verdict.rationale: Logseq's docs and branding position it as a privacy-first, local knowledge base with journals/pages and export to standard Markdown/JSON/EDN, implying local file ownership, and community users confirm using local git/GitHub sync for their markdown files (logseq-comm-1, logseq-comm-16). However, concrete community reports contradict the 'own local files, readable without the app' promise for the newer DB-based version: users say 'I can no longer keep all my data as markdown files' (logseq-comm-14) and note markdown export quirks that break compatibility with other tools (logseq-comm-19), plus past data-loss issues (logseq-comm-3) and unreliable early sync (logseq-comm-8). missing for 10: confirmation that the current default (non-legacy) version still stores everything as plain local markdown, resolution of the data-loss/compatibility complaints, and independent verification of full offline functionality.
